title: Halcyon Drift Rising Again
premise: On the terraforming colony Halcyon Drift, Ansel Fairweather is the last caretaker of a seed-vault garden meant for the colonists still sleeping in cryo. When he discovers that the orbital archive lists a ship that never flew—and his own name forged on its manifest—he uncovers a decades-old conspiracy: the colony's founding families rigged the wake-order to revive only their own bloodlines, leaving everyone else to die in their sleep. As the cryo-racks begin failing and Ansel's own memories prove to be edited implants of a man who never existed, he must choose between reviving the heirs who will restore a corrupt order and the strangers whose only inheritance is the truth. In the end, Ansel wakes neither faction's chosen list but a mixed first generation bound by the garden itself, sacrificing his implanted identity to become the colony's memory rather than its master.
about_author: Juniper Oyelaran is a former botanical archivist who spent six years cataloguing heirloom seeds in a decommissioned Arctic vault before turning to fiction. She writes slow-burning science fiction about inheritance, gardens, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Ansel Fairweather tends the seed-vault garden alone, recording daily logs for colonists still in cryosleep. His POV establishes quiet devotion and creeping loneliness; a routine inventory shows the wake-schedule countdown has quietly stopped moving. Emotional beat: tender routine shadowed by the first hint that someone, somewhere, has stopped keeping a promise.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Cross-checking the orbital manifest against his garden's supply ledgers, Ansel finds the freighter Meridian's Wake listed as departed—yet it never launched, and his own name appears as its registered pilot in handwriting that is almost his. POV: Ansel. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread as the colony's tidy records reveal a seam.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: Ansel descends into the cryo-bay to ask the waking technician, Odile Sarr, about the manifest. She denies everything too quickly, and he glimpses a rack labeled with names absent from every official colony roster. POV: Ansel. Beat: first human friction; the colony's silence becomes something deliberate and watched.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the sealed archive, Ansel finds the founding families' private ledger: a wake-order ranking colonists by bloodline, with the rest marked 'deferrable.' His forged pilot's license is filed there, dated three years before he remembers arriving. POV: Ansel. Beat: the vertigo of discovering your own history is a document someone wrote.

chapters.title: What the Plants Remember
chapters.summary: Ansel tests his memories against the garden's growth records and finds gaps: seasons he 'remembers' that never occurred, harvests logged in his hand he can't recall making. He begins recording everything on paper the archive can't edit. POV: Ansel. Beat: grief for a self that may be borrowed, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile confronts Ansel, revealing she's been secretly keeping a second, unranked wake-list alive in the system—her brother is on it. She offers to help him expose the ledger if he helps her wake her brother before the failing racks do. POV: Odile. Beat: wary alliance; two kinds of love for two kinds of family.

chapters.title: The Heirs Awake Early
chapters.summary: Someone triggers an unauthorized early wake of three founding-family heirs, led by the magnetic Cassian Voss-Adeyemi, who greets Ansel like an old friend Ansel has never met. POV: Cassian. Beat: charm as a weapon; the reader feels the pull of power even as Ansel doesn't trust it.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Cassian shows Ansel the hard truth: power reserves can now wake only half the sleepers. The ledger's ranked list is the 'responsible' choice, he argues—and Ansel's forged name proves he was always meant to be its executor. POV: Cassian. Beat: temptation framed as duty; the corruption theme turns personal.

chapters.title: Rust in the Racks
chapters.summary: A cryo-rack fails, killing forty sleepers before Odile can intervene. The heirs blame sabotage; Odile's access logs are wiped. POV: Odile. Beat: fury and fear; the abstract moral dilemma starts costing actual lives.

chapters.title: The Man in Ansel's Mirror
chapters.summary: Digging into the Meridian's Wake's true cargo, Ansel finds a cryo-cradle hidden in the ship's hold containing a body: the original Ansel Fairweather, dead for a decade. He is a copy, an implanted steward built to keep the garden—and the lie—running. POV: Ansel. Beat: identity collapse; the book's memory theme detonates.

chapters.title: Whose Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ansel confronts Cassian, who admits the heirs built 'Ansel' as a compliant caretaker and never expected the copy to start asking questions. Cassian offers him full recognition as a real man—in exchange for signing the ranked wake-order. POV: Ansel. Beat: the cruelest offer: personhood as payment for complicity.

chapters.title: The Garden Revolt
chapters.summary: Odile and Ansel broadcast the ledger to the waking colonists, but Cassian's faction seizes the comms tower and reframes it as terrorist forgery. The colony splits into camps. POV: Odile. Beat: truth is necessary but not sufficient; power controls the story, not just the switches.

chapters.title: Seed Vault Siege
chapters.summary: Heir enforcers come for the garden's independent power tap, the last resource outside their control. Ansel defends it with the only leverage he has: the vault's failsafe that vents the atmosphere and kills every seed—and the heirs' future food supply. POV: Ansel. Beat: the gentle caretaker discovers he can be dangerous; stalemate.

chapters.title: The Third List
chapters.summary: In the Meridian's Wake's hidden hold, Odile finds the original engineer's true plan: a third wake-list, drawn by lottery from all colonists, which the founders buried. It requires a registered pilot's signature—Ansel's forged identity is, horribly, the only valid key. POV: Odile. Beat: hope with a hook in it.

chapters.title: Cassian's Confession
chapters.summary: Cassian, rattled by the rack failures accelerating, privately admits the ranked list was never about resources—it was his grandmother's covenant, and questioning it has cost him everything he was raised to be. POV: Cassian. Beat: the antagonist humanized; inheritance as a cage even for its beneficiaries.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Dark
chapters.summary: The main reactor begins an uncontrolled shutdown; within seventy hours the cryo-racks fail entirely and everyone sleeps forever. All three factions must negotiate while the colony literally dims around them. POV: rotating—Ansel, Odile, Cassian. Beat: urgency compresses every grudge into a single room.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Cassian offers a final trade: he'll restore power and accept the lottery list if Ansel publicly validates the ranked list as a legal 'precedent,' preserving the heirs' honor. Ansel refuses to buy lives with a lie; Odile proposes instead that Ansel sign as the ship's pilot—truthfully, at last, as himself. POV: Ansel. Beat: the moral climax's hinge: identity claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: Meridian's Wake
chapters.summary: Ansel signs the third list under his own contested name and launches the never-flown ship's systems remotely to reroute power to the racks. The garden goes dark to keep the sleepers alive—the caretaker kills what he was made to tend. POV: Ansel. Beat: sacrifice of purpose and of the self he loved being.

chapters.title: What Wakes First
chapters.summary: The first lottery revival succeeds: a hundred strangers, heirs and laborers' descendants together, wake into a dying garden and must plant it themselves. Cassian, stripped of his list, chooses to stay awake and work the soil rather than sleep above the fray. POV: Cassian. Beat: power renounced becomes the beginning of repair.

chapters.title: The Archive Trial
chapters.summary: The awakened colonists put the ledger—and Ansel's nature—on trial. Odile defends the copy as a person; the heirs' lawyer argues a forged man can hold nothing, not even a name. Ansel testifies by reading his paper logs aloud. POV: Ansel. Beat: memory and personhood judged in public; dignity without a verdict guaranteed.

chapters.title: Halcyon Drift, Rising
chapters.summary: The colony votes: the lottery list stands, the ledger is sealed as evidence, and Ansel is confirmed as a legal person and the colony's Keeper of Records—the living archive no one can edit. Odile's brother wakes and plants the first new row. POV: Odile. Beat: justice as a garden, tended rather than won.

chapters.title: A Log for the Living
chapters.summary: Ansel records his final entry not for the unborn but for the living, then plants the last seed from the vault in open soil—no more vault, no more waiting. He is no longer a copy of a dead man's duty, but the author of his own. POV: Ansel. Beat: quiet resolution; inheritance reclaimed as something you choose to carry forward.
